subject: Enforcement slice mismatch — remediation & credits for Helio Labs
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@heliolabs.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden 429s across project/region

Hi Ben / Monica,

We started seeing a surge of 429 responses from Redwood for our analytics ingestion last night (~02:00-04:00 UTC) and again this morning. Logged items show the majority are enforcement window rejects (429) tied to tenant mapping. Attached a small sample of request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether this is a client-side burst or something on your enforcement path?

Impact: our ingestion lag spiked to ~12 hours for the affected window and a downstream job failed. This is blocking our reporting cadence for Monday AM.

Thanks — please route to ops if needed.

Samir
Helio Labs — Platform Lead

Attachment: helios_sample_429s.txt (text, 18 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@heliolabs.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden 429s across project/region

Hi Samir — thanks for the logs and for flagging the concrete impact. We're on it.

Quick summary of what I’ve done so far:
- Opened an engineering ticket and forwarded your samples to on-call (Karthik is looped).
- Asked for an immediate catch-all to reduce false positives while we investigate (temporary cap override).
- Putting together a short remediation plan and credit proposal; will share within 24 hours.

Preliminary observation from our side: the 429s look concentrated on an "enforcement slice" that maps a legacy tenant alias to a different quota window than the canonical tenant ID. In plain terms: two identifiers for the same customer ended up split across enforcement groups, which made your traffic hit the wrong quota bucket.

Next steps (today):
1) Engineering will apply a one-hour temporary override to prevent additional customer-visible 429s.
2) We will validate and update your tenant->enforcement mapping to canonicalize aliases (I will send a CSV of the proposed mapping).
3) After mapping changes, we will run a targeted replay on a small sample to confirm behavior.
4) We'll provide a report and a proposed one-time credit for the impacted window.

I’ll attach the mapping CSV in the follow-up. If you can share a preferred 30–45 minute window for a remediation call, we’ll book it immediately.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@heliolabs.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden 429s across project/region

Hi Samir — sorry for the disruption. A couple of practical items so we can move fast:

- Can you confirm the canonical tenant ID you want us to map to and any legacy aliases? A quick table (alias -> canonical) in reply will do.
- Preferred remediation window (we recommend 09:00–12:00 PT tomorrow for a low-impact validation).
- Any compliance / change freeze constraints we should be aware of?

I'll coordinate scheduling and ensure Karthik has sign-off for the cap override. We will also include a short postmortem and relief calculation after validation.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: credit approval request for Helio Labs

Internal note — forwarding proposed relief and approval ask.

Summary: enforcement-slice mismatch caused ~2.3M tokens to be rejected in the 02:00–04:00 UTC window; customer impact is ingestion delay and a downstream failed job. Proposed customer relief = 10% of the impacted window bill (~$3,800) plus a service credit to be applied to next invoice. Also proposing a temporary cap override scheduled for 24 Jun 16:00 UTC (1 hour) while we push the mapping fix.

Attachments: ratecap_mapping.csv, temp-cap-override.yaml

Requesting Evelyn's approval to finalize the credit and authorize the override.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@heliolabs.io>, Priya Rao <priya@heliolabs.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Resolution: enforcement mapping corrected and credit applied

Hi Samir / Priya — follow-up with the actions we completed and next steps.

What we did
- Identified root cause: tenant alias->enforcement-group aliasing (enforcement slice mismatch) caused your traffic to be evaluated against an incorrect quota window.
- Implemented mapping fix: aliases mapped to canonical tenant ID; validation replay ran successfully against a sample of 10k requests.
- Temporary override: 1-hour cap override applied to prevent new customer-facing 429s during the migration window.
- Credit: a one-time billing credit of $3,800 approved and will appear on your next invoice. See attached PDF for approval record.

Attachments: credit-approval-20260625.pdf

Follow-ups
- Monica will schedule a short retrospective to walk through the mapping logic and ensure the aliasing rule is covered by our onboarding checklist.
- We’ll add a monitor to alert when traffic from multiple tenant identifiers diverges significantly from baseline (to catch similar splits earlier).

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the quick signal from your team which helped us contain the incident faster. If you’d like a recording of the replay or the exact mapping CSV, let me know and I’ll share.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
